fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Detached Structure; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain a clear travel path for emergency vehicles.
• Clear an area near the detached structure or open green space that emergency vehicles can use to turn around.
• Cut back dense vegetation that narrows or obscures the driveway so full vehicle width remains visible and passable.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and detached structure so responders can move on foot between the two buildings.
• Mark the driveway entrance width with posts or reflectors so drivers can judge clearance before committing to the drive.
• Trim shrubs and low tree branches in the landscaped area adjacent to the access drive to prevent them from blocking vehicle mirrors or overhead clearance.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Ground Vegetation; Open Terrain; Vegetation Near Structure; Long Driveway; Single Access Route; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the structure to increase open space between the plants and the building.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to reduce the chance of fire moving from tree to tree toward the building.
• Remove or mow tall ground vegetation within the immediate area surrounding the structure.
• Keep the driveway clear of overhanging branches and low-hanging limbs along its full length.
• Thin shrubs along the driveway edges to maintain a clear travel path for vehicles and emergency responders.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate from the main road, particularly along the long single access route.
• Maintain the existing open areas between vegetation and the structure by keeping them clear of new plant growth.
